title: Use your own web address
content:
## What you'll get

Your app starts with a free `yourappname.emergent.build` address. A custom domain replaces that with your own name - like `myapp.com` - so visitors see your brand in the address bar.

---

## Buying vs bringing your own

You have two paths:

- **Already own a domain?** (e.g., you bought `myapp.com` from Namecheap or GoDaddy) Skip ahead to the connection steps below.
- **Need to buy one?** Head to any domain registrar - Namecheap, Google Domains, Cloudflare - search for your name, and check out. You'll manage DNS records in the next step at that same site.

<Callout type="note" title="One-line DNS primer">
DNS is the internet phonebook - it tells browsers which server hosts your domain. Updating DNS records can take a few minutes to a couple of hours to reach everyone, so don't panic if your domain doesn't work instantly.
</Callout>

---

## Connect your domain

<Steps>
<Step title="Open the custom domain panel">
In your Emergent workspace, go to **Deployments** → **Custom Domain** and click **Add Custom Domain**. The panel will show you a dedicated IP address - copy it.
</Step>

<Step title="Add an A record">
Log in to your domain registrar (wherever you bought the domain). Find the DNS settings page and create a new **A record**:

- **Host / Name**: `@` (or leave blank)
- **Type**: `A`
- **Value**: paste the IP address from step 1
- **TTL**: `Auto` or `3600`

Save the record.
</Step>

<Step title="Add a CNAME for www">
Most visitors type `www.myapp.com`. Create a **CNAME record** so both versions work:

- **Host / Name**: `www`
- **Type**: `CNAME`
- **Value**: `myapp.com` (your root domain, no `http://`)
- **TTL**: `Auto` or `3600`

Save this record too.
</Step>

<Step title="Verify in Emergent">
Back in the custom domain panel, enter your domain (e.g., `myapp.com`) and click **Verify**. Emergent checks for the A record and will provision an SSL certificate automatically - usually within a few minutes, occasionally up to 24 hours if DNS is slow.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Callout type="info" title="Screenshot coming soon">
Screenshot to be added.
</Callout>

<Callout type="success" title="Both URLs work">
After DNS propagates, `https://myapp.com` and `https://www.myapp.com` will both load your app. Emergent automatically redirects one to the other so you don't end up with duplicate content.
</Callout>

---

## If your domain won't load

**Check your DNS records** - Use a tool like [dnschecker.org](https://dnschecker.org) to confirm the A record points to the Emergent IP and the CNAME points to your root domain. Fix any typos at your registrar.

**Wait a bit longer** - DNS can take 1-2 hours (rarely up to 48 hours) to update everywhere. Check again in an incognito window to rule out browser caching.

**Look at the status badge** - In the Emergent Deployments panel, your custom domain row shows **Pending**, **Active**, or **Error**. If it says **Error**, click **Details** to see what's blocking SSL (often a DNS mismatch).

**Clear your local cache** - Your computer remembers old DNS lookups. On Windows run `ipconfig /flushdns` in Command Prompt; on macOS run `sudo dscacheutil -flushcache` in Terminal.

<Callout type="tip" title="Registrar help">
Every DNS provider's dashboard looks different. If you can't find the A record or CNAME section, search "[your registrar name] add DNS record" - most have a step-by-step guide.
</Callout>

---
